blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust applied to Media & Entertainment. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Media economics are attention economics: commissioning, scheduling, promotion and rights all price against predicted engagement. Studios and broadcasters that industrialize audience intelligence and content-operations automation compound catalog value instead of renting it.

items: Embanked titles leak with catastrophic value loss; supply-chain security thin.
Linear, streaming, social and box-office data siloed; commissioning decisions anecdotal.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Compliance, Audit & Digital Trust, Cloud Security & Posture Management, AI Security & Model Protection from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Commissioning and audience analysis, Content localization/ops, Rights/royalty accounting) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — Privacy (CDPA/GDPR-class) among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Watermarking, access control and partner gating (leakage prevented)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Telecom, Media & Entertainment level this capability reads as: identity-centric access and segmentation across core functions (lateral movement eliminated in validation). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
